chunks: 368 - A group of scholars narrated to us from Abu Muhammad al-Talakbari on the authority of Abu Ali Muhammad ibn Himam, who said:

Al-Shari'i was known as Abu Muhammad. Harun said: I think his name was Hasan, and he was among the companions of Abul Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad, and then after him among the companions of Hasan ibn Ali, peace be upon them. He is the first to claim a position that Allah did not assign to him and he was not qualified for it. He lied about Allah and His Proofs (Hujjah), peace be upon them, and attributed to them what is not worthy of them and they are free from it. The Shia cursed him and turned away from him, and the Imam's decree (Tawqi') came out cursing him and declaring freedom from him. Harun said: Then words of disbelief and sacrilege were uttered by him. He said: And all these claimants, their lie is first directed at the Imam, claiming that they are his representatives, calling the weak to believe in them through such claims. Then the matter escalates for them to the claims of self-deification (Hallajiyah), as became famous from Abu Ja'far al-Shalmaghani and his like, peace be upon them all, with the constant curses of Allah upon them.

key_terms.أَبُو الْحَسَنِ عَلِيُّ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ: Abul Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad, the 10th Imam
key_terms.أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ الشَّلْمَغَانِيُّ: Abu Ja'far al-Shalmaghani, a known false claimant
key_terms.أَبُو مُحَمَّدٍ: Abu Muhammad, the kunya (patronymic) of Shari'i
key_terms.التَّوْقِيعُ: Tawqi', a written decree or signature from the Imam
key_terms.الشَّرِيعِيُّ: Al-Shari'i, a specific companion of the Imams
key_terms.الْإِلْحَادُ: Al-Ilhad, sacrilege or deviating from the truth
key_terms.الْحَسَنُ: Hasan, the probable name of Shari'i
key_terms.الْحَلَّاجِيَّةُ: Al-Hallajiyah, the doctrine of self-deification associated with al-Hallaj
key_terms.لَعَائِنُ اللَّهِ: La'inat Allah, the constant curses of Allah

ai.seo_question: Who was Shari'i and why did the Shia curse him?
ai.summary: This hadith from Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* identifies Shari'i as the archetypal false claimant who usurped a spiritual station not divinely granted, leading to his excommunication (*tawarrud*) by the Imams. It illustrates the evolutionary trajectory of *al-ghuraba* (strangers/false claimants), where initial claims of deputyship escalate into self-deification, a pattern notably mirrored by later figures like al-Shalmaghani.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 368 - A group of scholars narrated to us from Abu Muhammad Talakbari on the authority of Abu Ali Muhammad Ibn Himam, saying,

Shari’s patronymic was Abu Muhammad. Harun said: I think his name was Hasan and he was from the companions of Abul Hasan Ali Ibn Muhammad and then after him from the companions of Hasan Ibn Ali. He is the first to claim a position that Allah did not assign to him and he was not qualified for it. He blasphemed Allah and his Proofs (Hujjah), peace be on them, and attributed to them what is not worthy of them and they are disdainful thereof. The Shia cursed him and turned away from him in dislike. Harun says: Then words of disbelief and sacrilege were uttered by him. All such claimants, first, attribute lies to the Imam and claim that they are his representatives, calling the weak to believe in them through such pervert claims. Then they graduate up to the claims of self deification, like the words of Hallaj as expressed by Abu Ja’far Shalmaghani and his like. On all of them be the constant curse of Allah.
